statement:
Boolean intervals: the complete list of stable types
Let $\mathcal G_{g,n}$ be the poset of isomorphism classes of connected stable weighted graphs with $n$ labelled legs, ordered by $H\leq G$ when $G$ is a contraction of $H$. Every interval is Boolean precisely for the stable types
\[
 (g,n)=(0,n),\quad n\geq3,\qquad\text{and}\qquad(g,n)=(1,1).
\]
For $g=0$ the order-reversing map from a graph to its set of internal-edge splits identifies this poset with the face poset of the complex of compatible stable splits, including the empty face.
This decides Part A(a)(i),(ii) and the first determination requested there; it addresses cote 150, scans 28--30.
notes: Complete stable-type list; graph enumeration is exhaustive from vertex/edge bounds.

statement:
Infima of pairs with a common lower bound
Every pair in $\mathcal G_{g,n}$ having a common lower bound has an infimum precisely for
\[
 g=0,\ n\geq3;\qquad g=1,\ 1\leq n\leq3;\qquad(g,n)=(2,0).
\]
In particular the two divisors $\Delta_{\mathrm{irr}}$ and $\Delta_1$ in type $(2,1)$ have two distinct maximal common lower bounds. The infimum assertion and the Boolean assertion therefore have different lists, related by the explicit graph constructions below.
notes: Complete infimum list, uniform counterexamples, exhaustive certificates in the four positive-genus cases.

statement:
Intersection and the Boolean deployment of a fixed contraction
For closed strata $X_G$ one has
\[
 X_G\cap X_{G'}=\bigcup_{H\leq G,\ H\leq G'}X_H.
\]
For a specified contraction $f:G\to G/C$, its intermediate factorizations, modulo isomorphisms of the intermediate graph commuting with both arrows, form the Boolean poset of subsets of $C$. This assertion holds in every stable type, including those excluded in A.1.
notes: The graph and the contraction are fixed before the factorization quotient.

statement:
The category with graph objects and its associative composition
Choose a multicurve $\sigma_G$ of each dual-graph type $G$. Define
\[
 \Hom_{\mathfrak M(g,n)}(G,H)
 =\{a\in\Gamma:a\sigma_G\supseteq\sigma_H\}/\Delta_{\sigma_G},
 \qquad [b]\circ[a]=[ba].
\]
This defines an EI category. Different choices of the $\sigma_G$ give equivalent categories by explicitly specified conjugation functors. The category on all multicurves with the same formula is equivalent to this finite-object skeleton.
notes: Right transporter cosets; explicit conjugation functors for changes of representatives.

statement:
Pinned strata, asphericity, and injective meridian lattices
For a stable graph $G$ with half-edge/leg set $I_v$ at vertex $v$, simultaneous normalization gives an equivalence of analytic stacks
\[
 M_G\simeq\prod_{v\in V(G)}\mathcal M_{g_v,I_v}.
\]
The unpinned stratum is $[M_G/\Aut G]$. It is aspherical as a stack, and for a multicurve $\sigma$ with graph $G$,
\[
 \pi_1([M_G/\Aut G])\cong\Stab_\Gamma(\sigma)/\Delta_\sigma,
 \qquad \Delta_\sigma\cong\Z^{\sigma}.
\]
In particular the meridian lattice injects in the open mapping class group. The extension of cote 147, (103), scan 80, has the asserted initial $1$ for every relative set of nodes. This proves (95), with its stated outer ambiguity.

notes: All stable types, stack asphericity, independent twist lattice and the initial 1.

statement:
The exact arrow-groupoid comparison and the pinning restriction
Let $\sigma\supseteq\tau$, put $S_{\sigma,\tau}=\Stab(\sigma)\cap\Stab(\tau)$, and let $a=[1]:\sigma\to\tau$ be the associated exit arrow. In the groupoid of arrows and invertible endpoint squares, its automorphism group is
\[
 \Aut(a)=S_{\sigma,\tau}/\Delta_\tau.
\]
The source and target functors induce respectively
\[
 S_{\sigma,\tau}/\Delta_\tau\longrightarrow
 S_{\sigma,\tau}/\Delta_\sigma\subseteq\Stab(\sigma)/\Delta_\sigma,
 \qquad
 S_{\sigma,\tau}/\Delta_\tau\hookrightarrow\Stab(\tau)/\Delta_\tau.
\]
The first map has kernel $\Delta_\sigma/\Delta_\tau=\Z^{\sigma\setminus\tau}$. These are the maps $\varphi$ and $\gamma$ in (103) for the unpinned incidence. For a target pinned by $G'$, replace $S_{\sigma,\tau}$ everywhere by the inverse image of $\Gamma^!_{G,G'}$, equivalently by the subgroup inducing the identity on the target dual graph. Fully pinning the source imposes the additional identity action on $G$. The corresponding restrictions and inclusions give the comparison with the manuscript's differently pinned versions.

notes: Exact pinning subgroups and both endpoint maps; no identification of differently pinned groups.

statement:
The MDT category, full flags, and Jansen's theorem
The coherent generization system of (103), with its full flags, reconstructs the category of A.4. This category is equivalent to the exit-path $\infty$-category of the stable-graph stratification of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}^{\mathrm{an}}$, and its classifying space is the homotopy type of that stack. For a flag $\sigma_0\supseteq\cdots\supseteq\sigma_r$, the automorphism group of the corresponding composable chain is
\[
 \left(\bigcap_{i=0}^r\Stab(\sigma_i)\right)/\Delta_{\sigma_r}.
\]
The two-cartesian law for composable arrow groupoids gives (105); composition is the map forgetting intermediate objects. Forgetting an intermediate graph need not be an equivalence of mixed groupoids.

notes: Full flags give coherent composition. The composite-link forgetful map can have index two.

statement:
A finite criterion deciding each immersion in (98)
For a specified contraction $f:G\to G'$, the proper gluing map
\[
 [\widehat M_G/\Aut_{G'}G]\longrightarrow\widehat M_{G'}
\]
is a representable finite local closed immersion. For a refinement $h:H\to G'$, form the finite set
\[
 B_f(H,h)=\{p:H\to G:f p=h\}/\Aut_{G'}G.
\]
Here the graph $H$ and its pinning over $G'$ are fixed; we do not quotient this set by automorphisms of $H$. The gluing map is a closed immersion exactly when $|B_f(H,h)|\leq1$ for every refinement. This is a finite decision criterion for every $(g,n)$ and every $f$. Every such map is a closed immersion for genus zero and for $(1,1)$. In every other stable type some such map is only a local immersion, first in dimension two at $(1,2)$.
depends_on_doubtful_reading: See the reading register for scans 78,80,82,150/39
notes: Finite retained-node criterion; target-object pinning is fixed in the fibre and is not further divided by Aut(H).

statement:
Normalization variance and formula (146)
Strict normalization of a pinned stable graph induces an equivalence of its moduli stack; disjoint union induces the product equivalence (133). For a general normalization morphism $G'\to G$, the contravariant map on pinned moduli is, in the product coordinates of A.5, the projection to the selected vertex factors followed by the forgetful maps of their selected marked points. This proves (144), (146), and the reduction to (148), with natural isomorphisms commuting with relabelling.
notes: Strict normalization, component products, selected components/markings and diagram (146).

statement:
The precise interchange and clutching coherence
For disjoint sets of nodes $C,J$, smoothing $C$ and normalizing $J$ commute through the canonical identification of their component families and remaining sections. Forgetting marked points and then stabilizing gives the commuting functor square with every generization constructed in C.1 below. Clutching pairs of labelled sections, both on distinct components and on one component, and relabelling define the modular operations on the exit categories, with their canonical associativity and equivariance isomorphisms. All coherence diagrams commute. For genus-zero boundary inclusions this recovers the replete full cosieve in entrance variance; in higher genus the clutching normalization has exactly the incidence multiplicities of A.8.
notes: Canonical clutching comparisons; see A.15 for the complete domain of a graph interchange square.

statement:
The simultaneous raw-face assertions in Part A(e)
The definition of $\Sigma_{G_0\to\cdots\to G_k}$ as the corresponding face of the real oriented blow-up does not satisfy all of Part A(e)(i)--(v). With literal oriented faces, (ii) and (iv) already fail for $(0,4)$. With ordinary strata as the object spaces, a link-to-open map is not the boundary-face immersion asserted in (iii). The correct complete Segal space is
\[
 W_r=N\bigl(\Fun([r],\mathcal E_{g,n})^{\simeq}\bigr),
\]
with homotopy-cartesian concatenation maps. Its arrow components are the relative link groupoids of A.6, and its homotopy category is $\mathfrak M(g,n)$.

statement:
Local triviality of the whole deployed family and its lattice monodromy
Over each pinned stratum, the entire normal-crossings family of faces is locally trivial as a stratified family in the analytic topology. For the unpinned stratum, the monodromy of the node set and of its integral angular lattice is
\[
 \pi_1([M_G/\Aut G])\longrightarrow\Aut G
 \longrightarrow\operatorname{Perm}(E(G))
 \longrightarrow\operatorname{GL}(\Z^{E(G)}).
\]
It permutes the positive Dehn-twist generators. The normal line at an edge $e=\{h,h'\}$ is $T_h\otimes T_{h'}$, with first Chern class $-\psi_h-\psi_{h'}$ on the pinned product stratum. These classes describe the angular torus extensions; local triviality does not assert a global splitting.

statement:
A fixed unpinned flag need not give the cartesian square
For the unpinned incidence components, Part A(e)(i) fails even after
replacing raw oriented faces by their correct relative link groupoids.
At type $(3,0)$ a homotopy fibre product of two specified incidence
components has two connected components, while a specified full flag
selects one. The homotopy-cartesian formula holds for the disjoint union
of all matching full flags, as in A.7. It also holds with the matching
intermediate pinning retained.

statement:
Deriving ordinariness from the two local inputs
For every stable $(g,n)$, the asphericity and meridian injection in
A.5 imply that every exit mapping space is a disjoint union of
contractible components. This gives the application of EXIT\_ONE\_TYPE
P1b1 requested in added task 1, before invoking Jansen's global
identification. That identification supplies the explicit transporter
formula and its compatibility over all incidences.

notes: Explicit derivation of ordinariness from aspherical strata and injective relative lattices.

statement:
Exactly when graph normalization and contraction have a square
Let $j:G'\to G$ be a normalization morphism in the sense of cote 147,
and let $q:G\to G/C$ be a contraction. Put
$C'=j^{-1}(C)\cap E(G')$ and $H'=G'/C'$. A commutative square
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
G'\arrow[r,"j"]\arrow[d]&G\arrow[d,"q"]\\
H'\arrow[r,dashed,"\bar j"]&G/C
\end{tikzcd}
\]
with horizontal normalization morphisms exists exactly when the
following finite tests hold: the induced vertex map is injective,
the genus at every source vertex equals that at its image, and no
retained marked half-edge or leg of $H'$ has been erased by $q$.
The induced maps of the remaining labels must have the incidences
specified in the definition of a normalization morphism; this is
checked directly on the surviving half-edges. When these tests hold,
$\bar j$ is unique, and the associated normalization and relative
generization groupoids form a commuting square up to a canonical
isomorphism. The comparisons are coherent under further admissible
compositions. An unrestricted such square for every pair is false,
already for the strict normalization and smoothing of the single
loop in type $(1,1)$.
notes: Finite criterion for a normalization-contraction square; single-loop counterexample to an unrestricted square.

statement:
The framed torsor and its two quotients
For a pinned stable graph $G$, put
\[
 P_G=\prod_{j\in J(G),\,M_G} U(L_j),\qquad
 L_i=T_{x_i}C\quad(i\in I(G)),\qquad
 L_e=T_{x_h}C_{v(h)}\otimes T_{x_{\bar h}}C_{v(\bar h)}.
\]
Here $U(L)=L^{\times}/\mathbb R_{>0}$ is the oriented unit-ray circle
bundle; no Hermitian metric is required.  We write
$P_G^E=\prod_{e\in E(G)}U(L_e)$.  Choose a finite set $B_G$ in the
pinned stratum, a nonempty finite set of rays above each member of
$B_G$, and saturate the rays under
$\mu_G=\{\pm1\}^{J(G)}$.  Denote the resulting finite set by $D_G$.
When a graph action is required, take $B_G$ invariant and also
saturate $D_G$ under the finite group $\operatorname{Aut}(G)$.
For vertices of genus zero and valence three or four, the groupoid
\[
 \mathcal S_G:=\Pi_1(P_G,D_G)
\]
is a $\mu_G$-free $\mathbb Z^{J(G)}$-groupoid, and its internal lattice
acts freely on every nonempty Hom-set.  Its geometric quotients are
\[
 \mathcal S_G/(\mathbb Z^{I(G)},\mu_2^{I(G)})
       \simeq\Pi_1(P_G^E,\operatorname{im}D_G),
 \qquad
 \mathcal S_G/(\mathbb Z^{J(G)},\mu_G)
       \simeq\Pi_1(M_G,B_G).
 \tag{B.1}
\]
The first groupoid has the node-framed link group of Part A.  The
second has automorphism group $\prod_{v:\,|F_v|=4}F_2$.  After choices
of trivializations, the automorphism group of $\mathcal S_G$ is
\[
 \mathbb Z^{J(G)}\times\prod_{v:\,|F_v|=4}F_2.
 \tag{B.2}
\]
The direct-product splitting in (B.2) is not specified as
$\operatorname{Aut}(G)$-equivariant.
notes: Topological circle bundles, labelled pinned rational components; graph action obtained by invariant finite ray saturation. Exact flag-to-edge tensor map and both lattice/sign quotients.

statement:
The presentation actually written in scans 115--117
For a trivalent rational graph set $r=|J(G)|$.  The finite model of
cote 146, scans 114--117 (folios 113--116), has the $2^r$ objects of
the sign torsor $D_G=\prod_{j\in J(G)}\varepsilon_j$.  It has
$r2^r$ positive half-turn generators
\[
 u_{j,x}:x\longrightarrow\sigma_jx
 \quad(j\in J(G),\ x\in D_G).
\]
Its relations are the source-compatible commuting squares for two
different coordinates.  The commutation of the full-turn loops
$v_{j,x}=u_{j,\sigma_jx}u_{j,x}$ written on scan 117 follows from
these squares.  Equivalently,
\[
 \operatorname{Hom}(x,y)=
 \{m\in\mathbb Z^r:m\bmod2=y-x\},
 \tag{B.4}
\]
where addition gives composition and $m$ records displacement in
units of a half turn.  The loop lattice is $2\mathbb Z^r$, identified
with $\mathbb Z^r$ by $2e_j\mapsto e_j$.

statement:
The proposed equivalence before forgetting leg framings
The proposed equivalence $S_0\mathcal T_G\simeq S_A\Pi M_G$ without
quotienting the leg framings is false, already for the graph with
one trivalent rational vertex and three labelled legs.  The exact
comparison is the first functor in (B.1), whose kernel at every
object is $\mathbb Z^{I(G)}$.
notes: Counterexample (0,3): Z^3 versus trivial isotropy. Correct relation is the explicit leg lattice quotient B.1.

statement:
The genus-zero tree index and the chart counts
The category of reduced stable trees with a fixed individually
labelled leaf set, and specified edge contractions fixing those
labels, is equivalent to a finite poset.  On four and five leaves,
the numbers of trees by number of internal edges are respectively
$(1,3)$ and $(1,10,15)$.  For the disjoint union of their trivalent
charts, the scan 116 presentations have the following counts;
these counts precede any global identification of chart objects.
\[
\begin{array}{c|r|r|r|r|r}
 n&\text{charts}&r&\text{framed objects}&\text{half-turn generators}
       &\text{node-only objects / generators}\\\hline
 4&3&5&96&480&6\,/\,6\\
 5&15&7&1920&13440&60\,/\,120
\end{array}
\tag{B.5}
\]

statement:
Freeness does not follow from an unspecified finite colimit
The implication that a finite colimit of groupoids with a free
$\mu_2$-action on objects has a free action on objects is false.
Consequently that implication alone cannot justify the sentence
following the first formula of cote 146, scan 100.
notes: Finite equivariant coequalizer of the indiscrete two-object C2-groupoid has one fixed object. Addresses a general colimit inference, not a specified manuscript index.

statement:
An explicit obstruction for the boundary-incidence interpretation
Let $L$ be the boundary of a sufficiently small regular
neighbourhood of the boundary divisor in $\overline M_{0,5}$.  The
colimit of the fundamental groupoids of its circle-bundle pieces
and all their torus intersections presents $\Pi_1(L)$.  The inclusion
$L\to M_{0,5}$ does not induce an isomorphism of fundamental groups.
Thus this specified boundary-incidence colimit cannot be the
missing global presentation in scan 100.
notes: Specified boundary-incidence colimit gives an aspherical closed3-manifold group with H3=Z; M0,5 has a2-dimensional K(pi,1), H3=0. No attribution of that index to the manuscript.

statement:
The precise relation to the Lego groupoid
Let $\mathcal L(\Sigma)$ be the marking two-complex of
Bakalov--Kirillov with their moves and relations, and let $\Gamma$
be the mapping class group with the same orientation and boundary
conventions.  The groupoid with objects the markings and arrows
\[
 M\longrightarrow M':\quad (g,[p]),\qquad
 g\in\Gamma,\quad p:gM\leadsto M',
\]
is equivalent to $B\Gamma$ by $(g,[p])\mapsto g$.  With fixed labels
and capped boundary circles it gives the open groupoid
$B\Gamma_{0,n}$ in Part A.  The capping functor kills exactly the
central lattice of boundary twists.
notes: Exact equivariant marking groupoid functor to BΓ, with composition, capping map and boundary-twist kernel; BK Theorem4.9 reopened.

statement:
The complete finite colimit and the generator dictionary
The index category, transition functors, and relations giving the
literal general finite colimit of cote 146, scan 100 have not been
reconstructed here.  The trivalent fibre presentation B.2, the
four-valent product and its two quotients B.1, and the finite tree
index B.4 are proved.  A generator-by-generator comparison between
that unspecified colimit and the Lego presentation is not proved.
notes: The local four-point model is reconstructed by B.16–B.17. The literal general finite-index colimit and transition functors remain unresolved.

statement:
Finite presentation yields a finite colimit of elementary framed groupoids
For each pinned stable graph, its framed fundamental groupoid admits
a finite-colimit presentation in the category of groupoids with its
specified central lattice and finite sign action.  One may take the
elementary automorphism groups, after changing the central lattice,
to be $\mathbb Z^r$ and $\mathbb Z^r\times F_2$, the groups of the
three- and four-point rational pieces.  The arrows in this colimit
are the word maps specified below.  This proves existence of a
finite algebraic presentation of the asserted kind.  It does not
identify these word maps with the unfinished tree-indexed diagram
of scan 100.
notes: Finite colimit built from explicit word maps in central extensions, with identity object maps preserving free sign action. Establishes abstract existence, not the original tree diagram.

statement:
The two open groupoids and their leg-framed extensions
For complex curves with individually labelled markings,
\[
 \Gamma_{1,1}=\langle a,b\mid aba=bab,\ (ab)^6=1\rangle
                 \cong\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb Z),
 \tag{B.8}
\]
\[
 \Gamma_{1,2}=\langle a,b,c\mid aba=bab,\ bcb=cbc,
               \ ac=ca,\ (abc)^4=1\rangle.
 \tag{B.9}
\]
Thus $\Pi_1M_{1,n}$ is equivalent to the one-object groupoid on the
displayed group.  The groups of the unit tangent-ray bundles at
all marked points are respectively
\[
 H_{1,1}=\langle a,b\mid aba=bab\rangle,
       \qquad z_1=(ab)^6,
 \tag{B.10}
\]
and
\[
 H_{1,2}=\left\langle a,b,c,z_1,z_2\ \middle|\
 \begin{array}{l}
 aba=bab,\ bcb=cbc,\ ac=ca,\\
 z_1,z_2\text{ central},\ (abc)^4=z_1z_2
 \end{array}\right\rangle
 \cong B_4\times\mathbb Z.
 \tag{B.11}
\]
Here $z_i$ is the positive full turn at the $i$th marked point.
The capping maps are the quotients $z_i\mapsto1$.
notes: Γ1,1=B3/<(ab)^6>; Γ1,2=B4/<(abc)^4>; framed H1,1=B3, H1,2=B4×Z with δ^4=z1z2. Independent cubic/quartic quotient construction and LP chain words.

statement:
All boundary graph groups in these two types
For $(1,1)$ there is one boundary graph: a rational vertex with one
loop and one labelled leg.  Its pinned stratum is a point and its
mixed stratum is $BC_2$.  Put $h=(ab)^3$.  Its fully framed mixed
link group is
\[
 \langle a,h\mid[a,h]=1\rangle,\qquad z_1=h^2.
 \tag{B.12}
\]
Its node-only mixed link group is
$\langle a,h\mid[a,h]=1,h^2=1\rangle$.

For $(1,2)$ name the four boundary graph types as follows:
$N$ is a rational vertex with a loop and both legs;
$T$ is an elliptic vertex joined to a rational tail carrying both
legs; $C$ is a two-edge rational cycle with one labelled leg on
each vertex; and $D$ is a rational loop vertex joined to a rational
tail carrying both legs.  Write
\[
 s=aba,\quad\Delta=abcaba,\quad
 r=s^{-1}\Delta s,\quad q=(abc)^2,\quad h=(ab)^3,
 \quad d=h^2.
 \tag{B.13}
\]
The pinned stratum groups are $F_2$, $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)$,
$1$, $1$ for $N,T,C,D$, respectively.  The mixed stratum groups are
$C_2*\mathbb Z$, $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)$, $C_2$, $C_2$.
The following are presentations of their fully framed mixed link
groups; in every row $z_1,z_2$ are central:
\[
\begin{array}{c|l|l}
 \text{graph}&\text{generators and additional relations}
                   &\text{node twists}\\\hline
 N&a,c,r,z_1,z_2;\ [a,c]=[a,r]=1,\ r^2=z_1z_2&a\\
 T&a,b,z_1,z_2;\ aba=bab&d=(ab)^6\\
 C&a,c,q,z_1,z_2;\ [a,c]=1,\ qaq^{-1}=c,\ q^2=z_1z_2&a,c\\
 D&a,h,z_1,z_2;\ [a,h]=1&a,d=h^2
\end{array}
\tag{B.14}
\]
The pinned full-framing subgroups are the kernels of the graph
permutation: in rows $N,C,D$ the respective quotient maps send
$r,q,h$ to the nonidentity member of $C_2$, and all lattice
coordinates to the identity.  The graph group in row $T$ is
trivial.  The node-only link groups are obtained by $z_1=z_2=1$.
The mixed stratum groups are obtained by also killing the listed
node twists.
notes: All stable boundary graphs in(1,1),(1,2), pinned/mixed groups and full node-plus-leg-framed extensions. Finite graph involutions retained.

statement:
Generization on every boundary flag in the two small genera
The generization maps from the groups (B.12)--(B.14) to the open
framed groups are the inclusions specified by the words (B.13).
In $(1,2)$ the two nontrivial two-step flags, in addition to the
cycle flags, have maps
\[
 D\longrightarrow T:\quad a\mapsto a,\ h\mapsto(ab)^3,
 \qquad
 D\longrightarrow N:\quad a\mapsto a,\ h\mapsto ac^{-1}r,
 \tag{B.15}
\]
with $z_i\mapsto z_i$.  For $C\to N$ retaining the node $a$, the
arrow-stabilizer group is the subgroup
$\langle a,c,z_1,z_2\rangle$ of row $C$, and its map to row $N$ is
the identity on these named generators.  The other contraction is
its conjugate by $q$.  These maps compose to the maximal
generization maps.  After the lattice quotients in B.10 they give
the corresponding pinned and mixed groupoid spans of Part A.
notes: Explicit braid words for every low-type flag; cycle contractions restricted to their correct arrow stabilizers.12 Artin-action checks pass.

The nine vertex orbits and the corrected sixteen arrow orbits

\[

statement:
The smooth/topological surface comparison actually used
For a compact oriented surface with finitely many individually fixed points, the inclusion $\Diff^+(S;I)\to\Homeo^+(S;I)$ induces an isomorphism of component groups, compatible with forgetting points, cutting annuli, and the twist generators. For stable types their identity components are weakly contractible. The unstable identity-component homotopy types are $SO(3)$ for $(0,0)$, $S^1$ for $(0,1),(0,2)$, and the torus for $(1,0)$. These give, for tangent-framed punctures in the two spherical marked cases, the respective kernel maps
\[
 \Z\twoheadrightarrow0,
 \qquad \Z^2\twoheadrightarrow\Z^2/\langle(1,-1)\rangle.

statement:
Restriction to the open fibre and the automorphism comparison
Let $U_r=\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C)\setminus\{r\text{ labelled points}\}$, $r\geq3$, and give $\mathbb P^1$ the stratification by those points and their complement. Its strict completed exit category has one open object with group $\widehat\pi_r=\widehat F_{r-1}$, $r$ closed objects with trivial groups, and crossing sets $\widehat\pi_r/I_i$, where $I_i$ is the peripheral procyclic subgroup. Restriction to the open object induces an isomorphism
\[
 \operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{eq},I}(\widehat{\Exit}(\mathbb P^1,r))
 \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
 \Out_I(\widehat\pi_r).                                    \tag{C.3}
\]
The left group is autoequivalences modulo natural isomorphism, preserving the labelled closed objects; on both sides we impose the same common multiplier on the chosen positive inertia generators. Allowing permutation of the labels gives the corresponding permuting version. These fibre exit categories occur in the universal stable-curve functors. Formula (C.3) is the map relating LM3b's surface-group automorphisms to the completed categories in this paper.

statement:
An explicit full-profinite filling kernel in every spherical size
Let $r\geq3$, let $F=\widehat F(x,y_1,\ldots,y_{r-1})$, set $p=xy_1\cdots y_{r-1}$, and put $\bar F=F/\langle\!\langle x\rangle\!\rangle=\widehat F(y_1,\ldots,y_{r-1})$. Let $O_{r+1,x}$ consist of peripheral-preserving outer automorphisms of $F$ fixing the distinguished puncture $x$, with a common unit multiplier, and let $O_r$ be the analogous group on $\bar F$. Filling and normalized filling are continuous surjections
\[
 f_x:O_{r+1,x}\twoheadrightarrow O_r,
 \qquad\theta_x:O_{r+1,x}\twoheadrightarrow\Aut_I(\bar F).
\]
Let $K\cong\bar F$ be the point-pushing subgroup. Then
\[
 \ker f_x=Q_r\rtimes K,\qquad Q_r\ne1.                      \tag{C.4}
\]
The following word model specifies $Q_r$ without a kernel notation. Put $N=\langle\!\langle x\rangle\!\rangle$. Take tuples $(w_1,\ldots,w_{r-1},w_\infty)\in N^r$ satisfying
\[
 x\prod_{j=1}^{r-1}w_j^{-1}y_jw_j=w_\infty^{-1}p w_\infty,   \tag{C.5}
\]
and the finite test that, in every finite quotient $F\twoheadrightarrow H$,
the images of the following elements generate $H$:
\[
 x,\quad w_1^{-1}y_1w_1,\quad\ldots,\quad
 w_{r-1}^{-1}y_{r-1}w_{r-1}.
\]
Denote the substitution they define by $\alpha_w$. The product is
\[
 (w*v)_j=w_j\alpha_w(v_j),\qquad
 (w*v)_\infty=w_\infty\alpha_w(v_\infty).
\]
Quotient by simultaneous right multiplication of all $w_j,w_\infty$ by $x^a$, $a\in\widehat\Z$. With its quotient profinite topology this is $Q_r$. Thus (C.4)--(C.5) give, in particular, the kernels of the fillings $4\to3$ and $5\to4$ as explicit profinite groups.

statement:
What the three bridge groups contribute at $5\to4$

Their closed normal closure inside $K$ has quotient $C_2$. Their intersection with $Q_4$ is trivial. Thus their actual contribution to the filling kernel in (C.4) lies entirely in its geometric point-pushing factor. The extra factor $Q_3\ne1$ already occurs for $4\to3$, where C.2 gives no bridge group.

statement:
The nonorientable comparison and real-equivariant representatives
For a compact smooth nonorientable surface, the inclusion of
diffeomorphisms into homeomorphisms induces an isomorphism of
mapping-class groups, also with individually fixed marked points
and boundary fixed pointwise. For a closed nonorientable surface
$N_h$ with $h$ crosscaps, the unmarked identity components in both
categories have homotopy types
\[
 SO(3)\quad(h=1),\qquad S^1\quad(h=2),\qquad *\quad(h\geq3).
\]
With one fixed point $N_1$ has identity component of weak homotopy
type $S^1$; with at least two it is weakly contractible.
For $N_2$ with at least one fixed point, and for $N_h$ with
$h\geq3$ with any number of fixed points, it is weakly contractible.

Let $\tau$ be a specified smooth orientation-reversing involution
of an oriented compact surface, and retain a specified finite
$\tau$-invariant marking. The inclusion of the smooth centralizer
of $\tau$ into its topological centralizer induces an isomorphism
on component groups, with the same marking conditions. Quotient
and lift along $S\to S/\langle\tau\rangle$ give the comparison.

statement:

 L_{g,n}\longrightarrow\mathcal M_{g,n}^{\rm an}\simeq B\Gamma_{g,n}

\[
 g=0,\ n\geq6;\qquad g=1,\ n\geq3;\qquad g\geq2,\ n\geq0.

statement:
Depth three is the sharp uniform input for the end's one-type

statement:
Compactification independence of the two end constructions
For any compact Hausdorff compactification $U\subset X$ with $D=X\setminus U$, the archimedean punctured-neighborhood pro-space is canonically the end system $\{U\setminus K\}_{K\subset U\text{ compact}}$. For smooth proper normal-crossings pairs this pro-homotopy type is constant, with representative the rounded real-oriented-blow-up boundary. Over a trivially valued field $k$, a proper modification $X'\to X$ equal to the identity on $U$ induces an isomorphism
\[
 W(X',X'\setminus U)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }W(X,D),\qquad
 W(X,D)=X^{\beth}\setminus(U^{\beth}\cup D^{\beth}).
\]
For proper $X$, this space is $U^{\rm an}\setminus U^{\beth}$. Properness cannot be removed: the compactifications $\mathbb G_m\subset\mathbb A^1$ and $\mathbb G_m\subset\mathbb P^1$ give one and two punctured boundary tubes respectively.

statement:
The stronger all-genus rank-selected connectivity claim
For arbitrary stable $(g,n)$, the claim that $P_k$ is $(\min(k,h(g,n))-1)$-connected has not been established here. D.5 proves a uniform lower bound and D.6 settles every requested low type. Good projective pairs are Mori hyperbolic and their comparisons are log crepant
A good projective pair has no nonconstant algebraic map $\mathbb A^1\to S$ into any open stratum. For a simple normal-crossings boundary, $K_X+D$ is nef. For two such completions and a common smooth normal-crossings resolution $p:Z\to X$, $q:Z\to Y$, write $B=Z\setminus U$. Then

statement:
Theorem R for projective threefolds, with the factorization reference corrected
Two good smooth projective normal-crossings completions $(X,D)$ and $(Y,E)$ of the same smooth complex threefold $U$ admit a common good smooth projective completion $X_s$ such that $X_s\to X$ is a sequence of blow-ups of smooth closures of strata and $X_s\to Y$ is toroidal. They are joined over $U$ by a finite sequence of smooth stratal blow-ups and blow-downs through good projective pairs. This confirms Theorem~R of the attached review in its projective threefold scope.

statement:
All one-step stratal modifications of $\overline M_{0,6}$
There are exactly $210$ nontrivial labelled smooth stratal blow-ups of $\overline M_{0,6}$: $105$ along boundary curves and $105$ at boundary points. Under permutation of the six labels they form four orbits, of sizes $45,60,15,90$. There is no nontrivial one-step stratal blow-down from the standard pair to another smooth SNC pair. The associated maps of conical complexes are the star subdivisions at the chosen two- or three-dimensional cones, with new ray the sum of their primitive generators. Theorem D.9 consequently applies to every good smooth projective completion of $M_{0,6}$.

Profinite simple connectivity at level two and above
For every stable type and every $k\geq2$, the full level completion of $P_k$ has trivial profinite fundamental group. The completed $P_1$ is connected. For the full curve complex, the same simple-connectivity conclusion holds for $d\geq3$. Completing the discrete presentation from the complex of groups on $P_2$ gives the full profinite group $\widehat\Gamma_{g,n}$ as a profinite presentation, with generators furnished by strata of modular dimension at most one and additional gluing relations furnished in dimension two.

statement:
A printed low-complexity range in the profinite literature
For the unmodified disjointness complex, the full level completion of $\mathcal C_{0,5}$ has a nontrivial continuous $\mathbb Z/2$-valued first cohomology class, and hence nontrivial profinite fundamental group. Thus the bound $3g-3+n\geq2$ printed in Kent's Theorem~12 cannot hold for the complex defined there. The argument in D.11 proves the corrected range $3g-3+n\geq3$. The genus-zero case of the analogous printed range in Theorem~13 likewise requires this correction.

The proved procongruence range and the remaining scope
For $n\geq2$, $2g-2+(n-1)>0$, and $3g-3+n\geq3$, the procongruence curve complex has trivial profinite fundamental group. This follows from Kent's Theorem~13 with its proof restricted to the actual simply connected range. The present proof does not establish the stronger higher-connectivity claims for arbitrary procongruence $P_k$, nor does it infer the congruence subgroup property from this one complex.

statement:
All passports, cusp fields, Atkin--Lehner actions, and signatures
For each lambency in Cheng--Duncan--Harvey's Table~2, the following tables give the complete permutation cover $X_0(N)\to X(1)$, its cusps, the action of the subgroup $S$ of exact divisors, and the signature of $\Gamma_0(N)+S$. The signature convention is $(0;e_2,e_3;c)$: genus zero, $e_i$ elliptic points of order $i$, and $c$ cusps. The genus $g_0$ in the first table is that of $X_0(N)$ before taking the $S$-quotient. A cycle expression $a^b$ means $b$ cycles of length $a$.

These are signatures of the effective modular orbifold. The homomorphism $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)\to\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb Z)$ has kernel $\{\pm I\}$, which acts trivially on every dart. Pulling the effective quotient back through this central extension restores the moduli stack of elliptic curves: its generic inertia is $\mu_2$ and its elliptic inertia orders are $4$ and $6$. Thus the displayed finite cover and its unrigidified modular stack are related by that specified central gerbe.

statement:
The exact tripod comparison and the eta-product check
The normalization of $X_0(N)\times_{X(1)}X(2)$ has one component of degree $\mu$ over $X(2)$ for odd $N$, and three components, each of degree $\mu/3$, for even $N$. They are defined over $\mathbb Q$. The component containing the standard cusp is isomorphic to $X_0(4N)$ for odd $N$ and to $X_0(2N)$ for even $N$; the other components differ by permutation of the three tripod punctures. For $4\mid N$ there is also the direct cover $X_0(N)\to X_0(4)$ of degree $\mu/6$.

For all twenty-three rows the exact modular function $T^X=1/\eta_{\pi^X}$ is $S$-invariant and descends to a $\mathbb Q$-coordinate on $X_0(N)/S$, with a unique simple pole and expansion $q^{-1}-d^X+O(q)$. The attached computation supplies the full integral cusp divisor and coefficients through $q^{30}$. The assertions of genus zero and invariance follow from those exact divisors and modular transformation criteria, without an inference from a truncated series.

statement:
Canonical reconstruction from the supplied face and collar diagram
Let $\mathcal V$ be the real oriented blow-up of a smooth complex normal-crossings Deligne--Mumford pair $(\mathcal X,\mathcal D)$, with its full deployed face diagram, collars, and maps to the strata. Collapsing precisely the normal angular circles over the zero radial coordinates recovers $\mathcal X$ as a topological stack. Equivalently, the mapping-cylinder pushout
\[
 \widehat X=X^*\mathop{\amalg}_{\dot X} C(p)
\]
of cote~150, scans~32--35, performed successively on the deployed strata, gives this same stack. For the supplied data, the final isomorphism is canonical and independent of the order of a compatible induction.

For $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$, the fundamental groupoid is already that of the compactification after all open divisors have been attached to the open stratum. In the deepest-strata-first reconstruction starting from $\mathcal V$, it is already that groupoid after the first layer, consisting of all maximal-corner fibres. In both descriptions it is the connected simply connected groupoid. These are two explicitly related filtrations of the same final quotient.

statement:
The corrected maquette and its comparison fibres
Let $\mathsf G_{g,n}^{+}$ be the category of stable labelled graphs with at least one edge, with specified contractions and graph isomorphisms as morphisms. Define
\[
 \mathcal B_p=
 \{\,(G,\lambda):|E(G)|=p+1,\ 
       \lambda:E(G)\xrightarrow{\sim}\{0,\ldots,p\}\,\}/\cong .
\]
Relabelling gives the symmetric-group action; an injection of label sets gives a face by contracting precisely the omitted edges. Then $\mathcal B$ is a symmetric semisimplicial set, its realization is the boundary complex, and the map assigning the label weights to the edge lengths is a homeomorphism
\[
 |\mathcal B|\xrightarrow{\sim}\Delta_{g,n}.
\]
Here $\Delta_{g,n}$ is the space of stable tropical curves of total finite-edge length one. The category with the automorphisms retained has the explicit comparison
\[
 B\mathsf G_{g,n}^{+}\simeq
 \operatorname*{hocolim}_{(\mathsf G_{g,n}^{+})^{\rm op}}\Delta_G
 \longrightarrow
 \operatorname*{colim}_{(\mathsf G_{g,n}^{+})^{\rm op}}\Delta_G
 =\Delta_{g,n},\qquad
 \Delta_G=\{(\ell_e)\geq0:\sum\ell_e=1\}.
\]
The actual point fibre of this homotopy-colimit model over a metric graph $(G,\ell)$ has homotopy type $B\operatorname{Aut}(G,\ell)$. The map need not be a quasifibration; this assertion concerns its actual point fibres. Adding the zero-edge graph makes the full graph category contractible, since that graph is terminal.

The analytic boundary end has a compatible comparison to these models. Over a positive-length metric multicurve $(\sigma,\ell)$, the point fibre of its Borel-model map to $\Delta_{g,n}$ is
$B\operatorname{Stab}_{\Gamma_{g,n}}(\sigma,\ell)$.
The map of that fibre to the graph-model fibre is induced by the graph-action homomorphism, whose kernel is the node-framed pure cut-surface group. In particular its homotopy fibre is the classifying space of that kernel.

statement:
The strict completion and its finite representations
For every stable $(g,n)$, set
\[
 \widehat C_{g,n}=\varprojlim_R C_{g,n}/R,
\]
where $R$ ranges over finite-index congruences on all Hom-sets, with the
object set fixed.  Composition makes this a category internal to
profinite sets, and restriction along $C_{g,n}\longrightarrow\widehat
C_{g,n}$ is an equivalence
\[
 \operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{cts}}(\widehat C_{g,n},\mathrm{FinSet})
       \simeq \operatorname{Fun}(C_{g,n},\mathrm{FinSet}).       \tag{E.1}
\]
Every functor between two such finite-object categories extends to their
strict completions.  A natural transformation extends as well, and the
extensions preserve its equations.
notes: All stable types; no congruence subgroup property required.

statement:
Constructible finite coefficients in every stable type
Fix $\overline{\mathbb Q}\hookrightarrow\mathbb C$.  For every stable
$(g,n)$ there are equivalences, compatible with stalk functors,
\[
 \operatorname{Cons}_{\partial,\mathrm{fin}}
       ((\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})_{\overline{\mathbb Q},\mathrm{et}})
 \simeq
 \operatorname{Cons}_{\partial,\mathrm{fin}}
       ((\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})^{\mathrm{an}})
 \simeq
 \operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{cts}}(\widehat C_{g,n},\mathrm{FinSet}).
                                                               \tag{E.2}
\]
Here $\operatorname{Cons}_{\partial,\mathrm{fin}}$ means finite-stalk
sheaves locally constant on every topological-type stratum of the fixed
boundary stratification.  Jansen, Corollary 6.6 and Theorem 6.7, and
Barwick--Glasman--Haine, Proposition 12.6.4, give the inputs.
notes: Finite stalk sheaves, fixed boundary stratification, characteristic zero, stack atlas descent.

statement:
The proposed nonsolvable-centralizer obstruction to (E.2)
The claim in Part E(a) that the finite constructible-sheaf comparison
requires

isotropy group $H\cong\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbb F_7)$ is false as
a claimed necessary step.  Formula (E.2) holds there, with this isotropy
retained, by its descent proof.  It does not assert the displayed
centralizer identity.

statement:
Functorial arithmetic action and its faithfulness
Forgetting, clutching, and relabelling, with their specified
compatibility isomorphisms, induce functors on the strict completions.
The full completed system has a coherent continuous outer action of
$G_{\mathbb Q}=\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb Q}/\mathbb Q)$,
and the map to equivalence classes of its autoequivalences is injective.
At a rational normal-crossings tangential point, a compatible local
representative acts on the meridian lattice by
\[
 (t_e)_{e\in E(G)}\longmapsto
                 (t_e^{\chi(\sigma)})_{e\in E(G)} .           \tag{E.3}
\]
Changing geometric paths conjugates the simultaneous local action.

statement:
Primitive meridians and retracts at all five-point flags
Let $G=\pi_1(\mathcal M_{0,5})$.  For a multicurve $\sigma$ on the
labelled five-punctured sphere put $H_\sigma=\operatorname{Stab}_G(\sigma)$.
Every $H_\sigma$ is a retract of $G$.  For $|\sigma|=1$ it is
$\mathbb Z\times F_2$; for $|\sigma|=2$ it is $\mathbb Z^2$.
Every full flag of boundary strata has a connected lifting groupoid,
whose automorphism group is one of
\[
 G,\quad F_2,\quad \mathbb Z\times F_2,\quad
 \mathbb Z^2,\quad\mathbb Z,\quad 1.                         \tag{E.4}
\]
All these groups are good, and the finite categorical quotients induce
their full profinite topologies.
notes: 15 compatible pairs verified by integral left-inverse computation.

LM3b H.9 at five points

In particular it classifies the corresponding constructible sheaves
with $\pi$-finite values, with all higher gluing retained.

The AA selection in ANABELIAN E.14

Among the maximal closed subgroups satisfying the AA-property of
Hoshi--Mochizuki--Tsujimura, Definition 5.12, exactly one contains $c$;

statement:
The kernel for an automorphism of an extension
Let $1\to K\to E\to Q\to1$ be an exact sequence of finitely generated
profinite groups, with $Z(K)=Z(Q)=1$, and let
$\rho:Q\to\operatorname{Out}(K)$ be its outer monodromy.  Restriction
and passage to the quotient give an isomorphism
\[
 \ker\bigl(\operatorname{Out}(E;K)\longrightarrow
                    \operatorname{Out}(Q)\bigr)
       \simeq C_{\operatorname{Out}(K)}(\rho(Q)).             \tag{E.8}
\]
The same formula holds after imposing any invariant peripheral
condition on the restriction to $K$, by intersecting the right side
with the corresponding subgroup of $\operatorname{Out}(K)$.
notes: Kernel theorem for full profinite extensions; no monodromy injectivity hypothesis.

statement:
An explicit inertia-preserving GT lift to
the three-point elliptic group
Put $K=\widehat\pi_{1,2}$, $Q=\widehat\Gamma_{1,2}$ and
$E=\widehat\Gamma_{1,3}$, where all marks are ordered and the
map $E\to Q$ forgets the third mark.  The standard GT action on
$\widehat B_5$ induces a continuous homomorphism
\[
 \Psi:\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}\longrightarrow
           \operatorname{Out}(E;K)
                                                               \tag{E.10}
\]
whose quotient action on $Q=\widehat B_4/Z(\widehat B_4)$ is the
standard action of Minamide--Nakamura, Theorem~4.3(i).  Its restriction
to $K$ fixes both cusp classes with the common multiplier $\lambda$,
and its action on $E$ preserves nonseparating twist inertia.

statement:
Automatic genus-one inertia: LM3b E.9
Let $A_{\rm per}$ be the subgroup of
$\operatorname{Out}(\widehat\Gamma_{1,3})$ preserving the kernel
$K=\widehat\pi_{1,2}$ of forgetting the third mark and permuting its
two peripheral subgroup conjugacy classes.  Then
\[
 A_{\rm per}=\langle\delta\rangle\times
                    \Psi(\widehat{\operatorname{GT}})
       \simeq C_2\times\widehat{\operatorname{GT}},          \tag{E.14}
\]
where $\delta$ interchanges the two original labels.  Every element
has one common peripheral exponent, normalizes $\langle\delta\rangle$,
and preserves nonseparating twist inertia.  Thus the group $A$ and
its subgroup $A^I$ in LM3b E.1/E.9 coincide, and
$A/\mathfrak S_2\simeq\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}$.
notes: Settles LM3b E.9 by the geometric-monodromy centralizer theorem plus explicit GT section; stronger peripheral subgroup condition suffices.

statement:
The two elliptic boundary maps and forgetting
Put $G_2=\widehat B_4/\langle\omega _4\rangle$ and
$G_1=\widehat B_3/\langle\omega _3^2\rangle$, where
$\omega _r=(\sigma _1\cdots\sigma _{r-1})^r$ and brackets on
central profinite subgroups mean closed subgroups.  Under the
geometric identifications $G_i=\widehat\Gamma_{1,i}$, forgetting
the second mark is
\[
 q:G_2\longrightarrow G_1,\qquad
 (\sigma _1,\sigma _2,\sigma _3)\longmapsto(a,b,a),
 \quad a=\sigma _1,\ b=\sigma _2\text{ in }G_1.       \tag{E.16}
\]
The rational-tail boundary has stabilizer $\widehat B_3\subset G_2$,
twist $\omega _3^2$, and normalization group $G_1$.
For the nonseparating twist $a=\sigma _1\in G_2$, put
$v=\sigma _2\sigma _1^2\sigma _2$ and $d=\sigma _3$.
Its stabilizer $H_a$ is generated by $a,v,d$ and satisfies
\[
 [a,v]=[a,d]=1,\qquad (vd)^2=(dv)^2,\qquad
                    a^2(vd)^2=1.                         \tag{E.17}
\]
Consequently
\[
 H_a/\langle a\rangle\simeq
 \widehat A_3/\langle\omega _3\rangle,
 \quad A_3=\langle\sigma _1^2,\sigma _2\rangle\subset B_3,
                                                               \tag{E.18}
\]
with $\sigma _1^2\mapsto v$ and $\sigma _2\mapsto d$.
This is the fundamental group of
$\mathcal M_{0,\{1,2\},[+,-]}$, the four-point normalization
with its two node branches unordered.  Its geometric branch
character is $v\mapsto1$, $d\mapsto0$ in $C_2$.
For every
$F=(\lambda,f)\in\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}$, the genuine
braid actions commute with (E.16), with the rational-tail
quotient, and with (E.18), including its branch permutation.

statement:
The orbifold normalizer maps and their parameter
For $r=3,4$, put $F_r=\widehat F(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$ with its
$r+1$ peripheral classes, $D_r=F_r/\overline{\langle\!\langle
x_1^2,\ldots,x_r^2\rangle\!\rangle}$, and
$K_r=\ker(D_r\to C_2)$, every $x_i$ mapping to the
nonidentity element.  Then $K_3=\widehat\pi_{1,1}$ and
$K_4=\widehat\pi_{1,2}$.  Let $\mathcal A_r$ be the genuine
peripheral automorphism group fixing the infinity class, and
$\widetilde N_r$ the inverse image in $\mathcal A_r$ of the
normalizer of the full geometric sphere group
$\Sigma_{0,r+1}\subset\operatorname{Out}_{\rm lac}(F_r)$.
Quotient-and-restriction
\[
 \rho_r:\mathcal A_r\longrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}_{\rm lac}(K_r)
\]
sends $\widetilde N_r$ into the outer normalizer of the full
elliptic geometric group $\Sigma_{1,r-2}$.  It descends to the
normalizer quotients by these geometric groups and is the
identity on their standard $\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}$
parameters.  The analogous elliptic filling map has the same
parameter.  This settles the orbifold-normalizer portion of
LM3b E.4, with its specified maps.

statement:
The injectivity asserted in ANABELIAN E.13
Let $\mathscr H$ be the labelled and coloured category of
ANABELIAN E.8: its objects are oriented hyperbolic surfaces;
its generators are finite unramified covers and specified
puncture fillings; its relations are diagram isotopy and
equality of actual composite maps.  Complete a right mapping-class
orbit $S_u\backslash M_S$ to
$\overline{S_u}\backslash\widehat M_S$ and retain the finite
label-permutation quotients, all label-forgetting maps, and all
specified deletions.  Let $F$ be a continuous type-preserving
autoequivalence preserving this structure.  If its outer action
on every labelled and coloured genus-zero mapping class group
is trivial, its induced outer action on every
$\widehat M_{g,n}$, $2g-2+n>0$, is trivial.

Thus restriction is injective on the compatible families of
outer group automorphisms induced by these autoequivalences.
